subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Types of number, sets and powers/roots

questions.q: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explain: 61 has no factors other than 1 and itself, whereas 51=3×17, 57=3×19 and 91=7×13.

questions.q: In set notation, what does the symbol ∈ mean?
questions.explain: The symbol ∈ states that an object is a member (element) of a set.

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
questions.explain: 24 is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 6 and 8.

questions.q: For two sets A and B, which elements are described by A ∩ B?
options: Elements in both A and B
Elements in neither A nor B
questions.explain: The intersection A ∩ B contains only the elements common to both sets.

questions.q: What is 3/4 written as a percentage?
What is 0.25 written as a fraction in its lowest terms?
Which of these values is the largest?
questions.explain: Converting all to decimals gives 0.7, 0.6, 0.65 and 0.68, so 0.7 is greatest.

questions.q: What is the result of increasing 80 by 15%?
After a 20% increase, an item costs £60. What was its original price?
questions.explain: The new price is 120% of the original, so 60 ÷ 1.2 = £50.

questions.q: How is 3400 written in standard form?
questions.explain: Standard form requires a number between 1 and 10, and 3.4 × 1000 = 3400.

questions.q: For any non-zero value a, what is a⁰ equal to?
questions.explain: Any non-zero number raised to the power zero equals 1.

questions.q: Simplify 2³ × 2⁴ using the laws of indices.
questions.explain: When multiplying powers of the same base you add the indices: 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.q: Write 5 × 10⁻³ as an ordinary number.
questions.explain: A power of −3 moves the decimal point three places to the left, giving 0.005.

questions.q: Evaluate (2³)².
questions.explain: When raising a power to a power, multiply indices: 2⁶ = 64.

questions.q: Which of the following is √50 written in simplest surd form?
£60 is divided in the ratio 2:3. What is the smaller share?
questions.explain: There are 5 parts, so one part is £12 and the smaller share is 2 × £12 = £24.

questions.q: A car travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?
How many minutes are there in 2.5 hours?
Estimate 4.8 × 20.3 by rounding each value to 1 significant figure.
A length is measured as 12 cm to the nearest centimetre. What is its lower bound?
questions.explain: To the nearest cm, the true value lies within ±0.5 cm, so the lower bound is 11.5 cm.
